news.title: Trump at South Florida rally revives the idea of military intervention in Cuba after Iran
news.text: President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war, his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach to the nearby country.Trump first floated this idea earlier this year, but has not mentioned it in recent months. But he revived it in response to a shouted question from the crowd about the island nation. He was campaigning just days ahead of midterm elections in which voters have expressed concern about the impact the U.S. war on Iran has had on prices of goods from gas to groceries.“We’ll do a little stopover,” Trump said. “Actually, what we’re going to do with Cuba is, we’re going to come back from Iran. Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We’ll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They’ll raise up their hands. And then we’re going to send (Secretary of State) Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal.”Both Rubio and Trump have been bullish on action in Cuba, with Trump previously suggesting the country would "be next” in terms of intervention abroad, following the winding down of the Iran war he has long forecast but which has not yet happened.In May, he and Rubio raised the specter of U.S. military intervention in Cuba, a renewed threat that took on greater weight after the administration announced criminal charges against the island’s former leader, Raúl Castro. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that previous U.S. presidents had considered intervening in Cuba for decades but that “it looks like I’ll be the one that does it.”RELATED STORY | Trump rules out attacking Iran before November's midterm electionsRubio told reporters separately that Cuba has been a national security threat for years because of its ties to U.S. adversaries and that Trump is intent on addressing it. While saying the Trump administration wants to resolve differences with Cuba peacefully, Rubio voiced doubts that the U.S. could reach a diplomatic resolution with the island’s current government.Moments after Trump spoke at the rally, Rubio posted on social media that “now is the time” for action on Cuba, addressing his post “to those who seek to create positive change” and urging them “to seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA.”Rubio has not addressed Cuba in depth in public for several weeks, with his last comments coming in a Sept. 29 interview with Fox News host Sean Hannity.“The truth is Cuba has already fallen. It doesn’t have a functional economy and it’s governed by people who continue to preach about some revolution that has been dead for 20 years that’s never worked,” Rubio said, without alluding to any CIA operation.“We are hopeful that Cuba will choose a different path. We are hopeful … that there will be some people in there that open their eyes to the reality of what they’re facing,” he said. “We’re never going to allow Cuba to become a base of operation against American interests or pose a threat to our national security. On that we are abundantly clear.”FOREIGN POLICY NEWS | Trump endorses embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelectionRubio and other top Trump aides have met with Cuban officials in recent months to explore possible improvements in relations. But the U.S. side has come away unimpressed from those talks, leading to even more sanctions imposed on the Cuban government.During his address to the United Nations General Assembly last month, Trump said Rubio — son of Cuban immigrants, who has long taken a hard line against Cuba’s socialist leadership — was “deep into negotiations with Cuba,” saying he would “not allow a haven for foreign adversaries to threaten America on our own doorstep.”Days later, Trump told reporters that he anticipated that the two countries “will make a deal,” adding, “I don’t think we’ll need the military. Cuba is failing very badly.”Earlier this week, the two countries clashed at the United Nations as the Trump administration sought once again to build opposition for an upcoming annual vote condemning Washington’s decades-long economic embargo against Havana.Cuba has struggled since 2020 with an economic and energy crisis. Its gross domestic product has shrunk, and its 10 million residents have endured blackouts, food shortages and inflation. There have been waves of protests, and hundreds of thousands of Cubans have migrated, many to the United States.
news.summary: President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war.

news.title: 'We May Do Another Epic Fury': Turns Warns Iran Of Fresh Strikes If Deal Not Reached
news.text:
US President Donald Trump has warned Iran of the possibility of another American military strike if Tehran fails to reach a diplomatic agreement with Washington. Speaking at a campaign rally in Florida, Trump suggested that the US could launch "another little Epic Fury" if negotiations do not lead to a deal.
The president adopted a hardline stance towards Iran while highlighting his administration's national security record and criticising the Iranian leadership.
Trump Hints At Fresh Military Action Against Iran
"We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree," Trump told the cheering crowd, indicating that military action remained a possibility if diplomatic efforts failed.
Questioning Iran's willingness to negotiate, the US president said, "If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business.' But, you know, I doubt they'll do that because perhaps they're not smart."

news.title: Trump unveils $250 million elder care plan
news.text: Digital Desk | Washington, Oct 24 (IANS) US President Donald Trump has announced a $250 million initiative to recruit at least 5,000 nurses for elder care facilities across the United States, unveiling a new healthcare workforce measure as he campaigned for Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The announcement came during a political rally in Fort Myers, Florida, where Trump outlined a series of domestic policy measures. "And today I have breaking news for the benefit of American seniors," Trump told supporters. "But I'm pleased to announce that the Trump administration is investing $250 million to hire at least 5,000 new nurses in elder care facilities all across America." The President said the initiative would benefit facilities nationwide, including those in Florida, a state with a substantial elderly population. He did not provide details about how the money would be distributed, when recruitment would begin or which government agencies would administer the programme. The announcement also did not specify whether the funding would support permanent positions, temporary recruitment incentives or other measures intended to address staffing requirements. The initiative was announced in the presence of senior administration officials, including Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Dr Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. Trump praised both officials during the rally, highlighting their roles in his administration's healthcare agenda. He also spoke about efforts to reduce prescription drug prices through agreements with other countries. Trump claimed his administration had secured arrangements intended to bring American medicine prices closer to those charged abroad. "So, this will reduce drug prices by 50 to 90 percent," he said. The elder care announcement was among several policy initiatives Trump highlighted while campaigning for Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds and Senator Ashley Moody in Florida. Trump urged voters to return Republicans to both chambers of Congress, arguing that his administration needed continued legislative support to implement its priorities. He also used the rally to discuss taxation, immigration enforcement, manufacturing investment and measures intended to improve household finances. The healthcare workforce announcement stood apart from the broader campaign rhetoric because it identified a specific funding amount and recruitment target. Long-term care facilities in the United States provide residential and medical support to elderly people, including those requiring continuous nursing supervision, rehabilitation and assistance with daily activities. Staffing levels are an important factor in the quality and availability of such care.

news.title: Hero dad who bravely stopped Oregon school shooter says 'I'm sorry' to parents after tragedy
news.text: A heroic father who fatally shot a school shooter has apologised to the parents of the children he was unable to save. Kaylub Giamanco says he was the 'last line of defence' at Silver Rail Elementary in Oregon and, despite ultimately foiling the horrific attack, he regrets not arriving sooner and saving more lives. “I want to apologise for not saving their babies, that’s probably the biggest thing for me right now,” Giamanco said. “The gratitude for saving people’s children is awesome. But there were ones that I didn’t save.” Three children — ages 5, 8 and 11 — and a teacher were killed at the school in Bend, Oregon, last week when a former student there, 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, blasted his way through locked doors with a shotgun and attacked a special needs classroom. Another student was critically injured and a teacher was injured and hospitalised. Giamanco had dropped off his daughters at the school that morning before driving to work as normal. A few hours later, however, the 36-year-old carpenter found himself passing the school again as he was heading home for lunch - that was when he spotted someone wearing black and carrying a long gun. The man fired shots into a pickup truck and at a person mowing the school’s lawn, before climbing a fence and heading toward the school building. Giamanco said “panic fled into my brain.” He grabbed a .40-caliber handgun from his truck’s center console and went after the gunman as he dialed 911. He asked the dispatcher to send help before hanging up his phone. “I said ‘I’m sorry I have to go in. People are going to die,’” Giamanco said. As he got closer to the building, Giamanco said, he lay on his stomach and used his elbows to crawl across the ground. “That’s when I started hearing children pleading for their lives,” he said. “And then I started hearing gunfire and I just started army crawling faster and faster. And I told myself: ‘This is probably the last thing that I’m ever going to do.’” Giamanco said he entered the school through a window that had been shot out. Peeking into a nearby classroom, he saw a teacher grappling with the shooter. He said he faced them both in profile, giving him an open shot. “I felt like I was the last line of defense between him and the rest of the children,” Giamanco said. He swung the door open, stepped into the room and fired his gun. Police say another teacher threw her phone at the attacker and wrestled with him before Giamanco shot and killed him. Both the gunman and the teacher dropped to the floor. The teacher bolted from the room as the shooter reached for his shotgun. “He was scrambling for his weapon,” Giamanco said. “I looked at him and I shot him two more times to make sure that he couldn’t move, because I was afraid of him shooting anybody else.” Police have said Giamanco was carrying his gun legally in his truck and have credited him and the unarmed teacher who confronted the gunman with saving multiple lives. A day after the shootings, President Donald Trump hailed Giamanco was a “great hero” who “took care of business.” A second teacher in the classroom, Becky Drury, said in a statement Wednesday that she lay on the floor, helplessly playing dead, after being struck at close range by a shotgun blast that nearly severed her left hand. The teacher who struggled with the shooter hasn’t been publicly identified. Giamanco told the public broadcaster that she’s “a real true hero” whose actions gave him an opening to kill the attacker. “I can’t tell you what it feels like to take a life … but I can tell you that I genuinely feel like I was supposed to be there,” Giamanco said. “If I wasn’t there, I just don’t know what would have happened.”
news.summary: Three children aged five, eight and 11 were killed in the horror shooting, along with a teacher - Kaylub Giamanco has been hailed as a hero after fatally shooting 16-year-old Griffin J. John II.
news.author: Peter Hennessy

news.title: Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity celebrate upcoming wedding surrounded by family and friends at Mar-a-Lago
news.text: Fox News hosts Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity celebrated their upcoming wedding on Friday with a gathering of family, close friends and longtime colleagues at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida. The pre-wedding festivities brought together loved ones from different chapters of their lives for a special evening honoring the couple. "My heart is overflowing with gratitude and joy," Earhardt said. "To celebrate this beautiful season of our lives surrounded by the people we love most is truly a dream come true. God has blessed us in more ways than we could ever imagine, and I am so thankful that He brought Sean and me together. Our families, our children and our precious friends mean the world to us and sharing this moment with them makes it even more meaningful. We are so excited for this next chapter and know that the very best is yet to come." Earhardt, co-host of the network's top-rated morning program "FOX & Friends" and Hannity, the host of FOX News Channel's "Hannity" and podcast "Hang Out with Sean Hannity," announced their engagement in December 2024 after Hannity proposed over Christmas at their home church in Florida. "Ainsley is an incredible person and I couldn't be happier or more grateful that God brought us together," Hannity said. "Faith, family and friendship are what matter most in life and having so many people we love and care about together to celebrate this moment means the world to us. We are incredibly blessed and I can't thank everyone enough for being part of such a special evening." Among those celebrating were Fox News Media CEO Suzanne Scott and FOX News President and Executive Editor Jay Wallace as well as Earhardt's fellow "FOX & Friends" co-hosts Steve Doocy, Lawrence Jones and Brian Kilmeade, along with numerous other Fox News personalities. President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump were also in attendance, along with Eric and Lara Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his wife, Jeanette, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his wife, actress Cheryl Hines, Sen. Tim Scott, Sen. Darline Graham, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro, among others. "I've had a personal relationship with President Trump for over 30 years," Hannity said. "When Ainsley and I began planning this celebration, it was important to us that he could be part of this special time in our lives. We chose to host a party at Mar-a-Lago and paid fair market value for the venue. We are grateful that he and Melania could celebrate alongside our families and friends." Other guests included longtime friends of the couple, including ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith, country music legend Lee Greenwood, podcast host Sage Steele, television personality Jillian Michaels and Steve and Andrea Wynn. Both Earhardt and Hannity have longstanding careers at Fox News. Earhardt joined in 2007 and became a co-host of "FOX & Friends" in 2016 while Hannity has been with the network since its launch in 1996. The evening reflected the importance of faith, friendship and the relationships the couple has built over the years as they look forward to exchanging vows.
news.summary: Fox News hosts Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity celebrated their upcoming wedding on Friday with a gathering of family, close friends and longtime colleagues at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida.

news.title: AIPAC’s shift
news.text:
ON Wednesday, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) made an unusual announcement. The organisation would no longer endorse or make direct contributions to candidates running in US elections. This marks the end of a practice that AIPAC began in 2021 (its lobbying started in the ‘50s).

This does not mean that the Israel lobby will stop trying to influence US elections. AIPAC will continue mobilising individual donors. However, the announcement is an acknowledgement of the growing difficulties associated with overt affiliation with the lobby and the pro-Israel agenda. The genocide in Gaza and the war in Iran have created a situation where many Americans are questioning their country’s support for Israel and the resources devoted to it. Democratic candidates have challenged US involvement in the Middle East and the $3.8 billion in annual assistance Washington provides Israel.

No campaign has illustrated this with greater clarity than that of Dr Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for the US Senate seat in Michigan. In the Democratic primary, AIPAC spent $30 million backing El-Sayed’s opponent, Haley Stevens. Other political action committees also spent heavily on her campaign. In contrast, El-Sayed spent only $3.2m, most of it raised from individual donors.

Despite all this, El-Sayed won. One reason was his willingness to confront Stevens over AIPAC’s involvement in the race and to question why US taxpayer money should go to another country. What El-Sayed was able to do is connect two different realities of the American political context. First, he tapped into the American fatigue with interminable wars in the Middle East. Again, and again, he argued that the US had “no business” becoming embroiled in further conflicts, while infrastructure and institutions at home were decaying. His criticism of Donald Trump’s escapades in Iran became part of this argument. Second, El-Sayed connected the affordability crisis facing Americans to questions about government spending and the country’s relationship with Israel. Americans struggling to afford healthcare and basic groceries are naturally questioning how public money is spent abroad. 

 War-weary Americans can see through Israeli machinations.

El-Sayed is not campaigning on Israel alone. Affordability and healthcare are central issues for him, and he supports a government-funded Medicare For All option that would make healthcare accessible to millions of people. His own background in public health makes him a persuasive speaker on these issues. AIPAC’s affiliated Super PAC has now directed spending against El-Sayed in his contest with Republican Mike Rogers. This is a departure from AIPAC’s usual support for Democratic candidates in Michigan.

American Zionists and the well-heeled donors behind AIPAC may see the Michigan contest not simply as an electoral battle in a US state but also as an indicator of how anti-Israel sentiment is becoming increasingly pervasive among the Democratic electorate. The announcement that there will be no more overt endorsements reflects the liability that public association with AIPAC can create for some candidates. It is a sea change in the character of Democratic politics in the US. 

There are global implications in this shift. If El-Sayed wins — and one hopes he does despite the millions that AIPAC is now pouring into his opponent’s coffers — it will mean that other Democratic lawmakers in the House and Senate will have to think twice about voting to send billions of dollars to Israel. In the past, Democratic politicians have voted en masse for just these sorts of measures. 

Israel is very proud of its genocidal actions in Gaza. It is also quite smug about having persua-d--ed Trump to at--tack Iran. It sees both of these act-ions and its continuing excesses in Gaza and the West Bank as victories. This, however, is an illusion. The reality is that in the process of achieving the former, Israelis forgot that ordinary, war-weary Americans can see through its machinations. This is important not because Israel cares what Americans think but because Israel is entirely dependent on the US, receiving almost 70 per cent of its military equipment from them.

As the election of Zohran Mamdani in New York City and the hopeful rise of Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan show, Americans are signalling just how fed up they are with Israel’s intrusions in their own government and its attempts to create dual loyalties in their political leadership. As American leaders stop signing blank cheques for Israel as in the past five decades, Israel is likely to face enormous struggles. Already an isolated nation, increasingly detested by the world for the carnage of innocents, its future is not that of a victorious nation but of a widely reviled one. 

The writer is an attorney teaching constitutional law and political philosophy.

news.title: Asian football endorses Infantino’s re-election in apparent U-turn
news.text:
TOKYO: The head of Asian football on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president, weeks after stinging criticism over his aborted World Cup sell-off plan.

The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing, in a significant boost to Infantino’s prospects of extending his reign.

The AFC in August had joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, representing federations in North and Central America and the Caribbean, in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino has faced calls to quit and lost the support of some associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term.

“I think that we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as FIFA president,” said Sheikh Salman. “I think you’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent.

“I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear.” 

Hinting at previous discord, Sheikh Salman told the AFC Extra-ordinary Congress and Infantino: “Gianni, yes, we had some issues we spoke about in the past.

“But let’s not relate the two things together. We need to move forward... football is strongest when we work together.” 

Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March.

In response to the AFC’s backing, Infantino said: “We have seen the transformation that Asian football, and as a consequence world football, has gone through in these years.

“It has become truly global. It has become for everyone, and this would not have been possible without a strong, a united, a committed Asia. And for this, I thank you very much.” The deadline for candidates to decl-are for the election is Nov 18. No heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against Infa-ntino so far, despite outspoken cond-emnation, most notably from Europe.

Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino over controversies including his close relationship with US President Donald Trump.

Two months ago the AFC and Sheikh Salman signalled they could turn on Infantino.

A joint letter with UEFA and CONCACAF declared football “belongs to no individual”.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” the confederations said.

Infantino has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South Amer-ican governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive.

The confederations do not vote as blocs and there have been some supportive voices for Infantino from within CONCACAF.

AFC members Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar had previously backed him.

So too did the football federation of Saudi Arabia, which will host the 2034 World Cup.

news.title: Trump Tells Florida of Plans for USA to Topple Cuban Communist Regime
news.text:
President Donald Trump told a Florida crowd Friday that a U.S. warship could force Cuba’s communist government to surrender after Iran, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent to “finish up the deal.”

Trump made the remarks during a campaign rally at Alico Arena at Florida Gulf Coast University in Fort Myers after someone in the audience asked about Cuba.

“No, Cuba, he wants to know what about Cuba. Give me a break. Give me a break,” Trump said. “Don’t worry. We’ll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran. We’ll do a little stopover.”

Trump then described having American ships pass the island on their return from Iran, with one stopping just offshore.

“No, we’ll do a little stopover. Actually, what we’re going to do with Cuba is we’re going to come back from Iran. Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba,” he said.

“We’ll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They’ll raise up their hands. And then we’re going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal.”

Trump went on to suggest that Rubio could handle the task without the ships stopping.

“We’ll have Marco. We don’t even have to stop,” he said. “We could just put him in there and he’ll figure it out. He’s a great guy.”

Rubio, a former U.S. senator from Florida, has handled much of the administration’s Cuba policy. Trump has said he wants to fundamentally change the island’s communist government, increasing pressure on Havana during his second term.

In September, the administration announced additional sanctions targeting Cuban elites, financial channels and resource operations. The State Department accused the communist government of posing a threat to U.S. national security.

Rubio has also publicly questioned how long Cuba’s current system can survive. In an interview with Fox News host Sean Hannity, he described the country as a failure under leaders who continued to promote a revolution that had not worked.

Trump’s Florida appearance was intended to support Republican Rep. Byron Donalds in his campaign for governor against Democrat David Jolly. Cuba remains a major political issue in the state, where Cuban Americans are an influential voting bloc.
news.summary:
President Donald Trump told a Florida crowd Friday that a U.S. warship could force Cuba’s communist government to surrender after Iran, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent to “finish up the deal.”

news.title: Trump says Putin freed American after his call
news.text: Digital Desk | Washington, Oct 24 (IANS) US President Donald Trump has said Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to release American citizen Stephen Hubbard following a personal telephone request, describing the development as a diplomatic success amid continuing tensions between Washington and Moscow over the war in Ukraine. Speaking at a Republican campaign rally in Fort Myers, Florida, Trump said Hubbard had returned to the United States after spending years in Russian custody. The President claimed he raised the case directly with Putin during a telephone conversation on Friday and secured an immediate commitment to release the American. "I called Vladimir Putin on Friday and I said, will you do me a favour? Give me the person you have named Stephen Hubbard, give him back to me, would you, please?" Trump told supporters. According to Trump, the Russian leader agreed. "And he said, I will do that," Trump said. The President said Hubbard had since arrived in the United States and reunited with his family. "And he gave him back to us. And he just arrived in our country and it's great, it's great. His family is very happy," he said. Trump offered no details about the arrangements surrounding Hubbard's release, including whether Moscow received any concessions or whether other diplomatic channels were involved. He also did not disclose the precise date of Hubbard's return or identify the American officials who helped coordinate the transfer. The President presented the release as an example of his ability to secure results through direct engagement with foreign leaders. He criticised the previous administration of President Joe Biden, arguing that Hubbard should have been brought home much earlier. "It was under Biden that they took him, he should have gotten him back that night, the night they took him," Trump said. The President said Hubbard's son had made a strong impression on him during efforts to secure his father's freedom. "I saw Stephen Hubbard's son; he made a great impression. He really wanted to get his father; he was in Russia for years," Trump said. He described the American's experience in Russian custody as difficult and suggested the family had endured a prolonged period of uncertainty. The remarks came as Trump discussed his broader foreign policy record, including efforts to negotiate an end to the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Trump said he remained hopeful that the war could be brought to a conclusion. "We're close to ending, I hope, the Russia-Ukraine catastrophe. I hope we're ending that," he told the rally. The President also cited what he described as the continuing human cost of the fighting, claiming that an average of 25,000 soldiers were being killed each month. Trump did not indicate whether Hubbard's release was connected to wider negotiations involving Russia and Ukraine. The release, as described by Trump, would represent a separate humanitarian development in the US-Russia relationship, even as Washington and Moscow remain divided over the conflict in Ukraine. Russia's detention of American citizens has been a recurring source of diplomatic friction. Previous cases have prompted negotiations over prisoner exchanges and the conditions under which detained Americans can return home.

news.title: Russia sends three diesel tankers toward US
news.text:
Russia has dispatched three tankers carrying diesel fuel toward the United States under an agreement reached between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his American counterpart Donald Trump, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has announced.

The vessels are already sailing toward the eastern Atlantic coast, Novak said on Friday, adding that most of the additional fuel supplies could come from Russian energy giant Rosneft.

“In accordance with the previously announced agreements to saturate the global diesel market, Russia will ensure additional supplies of diesel fuel to world markets and the United States,” Novak said.

Moscow has eased its restrictions on diesel exports, allowing Russian companies to ship up to 500,000 tons of fuel to international markets in October while ensuring domestic demand remains fully covered. The shipments were arranged with significant assistance from the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF), headed by Putin’s economic envoy Kirill Dmitriev.

Further deliveries would continue on a regular basis, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said earlier in the day, confirming that the first tanker had departed for its buyers but not identifying the vessel.

Maritime tracking groups identified one of the tankers as the Malta-flagged Agioi Fanendes, carrying approximately 40,000 tons of diesel. Reuters reported that the vessel had departed Russia’s Baltic port of Primorsk and was heading toward New York, with an initial estimated arrival date of November 7.

TankerTrackers reported a total of three vessels that had loaded diesel at Russian terminals and were declaring the United States as their destination. However, the identities of the vessels and their final discharge ports have not yet been publicly confirmed.

The deliveries follow an October 9 phone conversation between Putin and Trump, after which the American president announced that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by 500,000 tons in November, another million tons shortly thereafter, and potentially further shipments depending on refining capacity. Washington subsequently issued a temporary sanctions waiver permitting Russian diesel imports, reversing restrictions introduced under former President Joe Biden in 2022.

The agreement comes as Trump faces mounting pressure to bring down fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. US diesel prices surged above $6.50 per gallon in September, with prices in parts of California exceeding $8, amid disruptions to global energy supplies caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran and restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Russia has historically been the world’s second-largest diesel exporter, behind only the US, accounting for roughly 10% of global exports. Disruptions to Russian supplies can drive up prices even in countries that do not directly import the fuel.

Trump has repeatedly urged Ukraine’s Vladimir Zelensky to stop attacking Russian refineries, accusing Kiev of exacerbating the worldwide diesel shortage and hurting American consumers and farmers.

Zelensky rejected the criticism on Thursday, calling Trump’s claims “totally false” and accusing the American leader of “deflecting the focus away from Iran.”
news.summary:
Deputy PM Alexander Novak has confirmed the first shipments under an agreement with Washington aimed at easing the global fuel crisis

news.title: Indian-American Amish Shah faces Trump’s golf partner in Arizona swing seat
news.text: Digital Desk | Washington, Oct 24 (IANS) Indian-American Democrat Amish Shah is up against a Republican who has been a friend and golf partner of President Donald Trump for decades, as Trump and his allies make a late push in the Arizona congressional race. “President Donald Trump and his allies are mounting a last-minute mission to shore up his longtime personal friend in a battleground Arizona district,” Politico said on Friday in a report headlined “Meet Trump’s favorite House Republican candidate”. The president has known former NFL kicker Jay Feely “for decades as a friend and golf partner, and he sees the former Arizona Cardinals kicker as a formidable candidate,” the report said, citing two Trump officials familiar with their relationship. It said GOP groups have spent more than $22 million to boost Feely, much of it in the final weeks. Shah, an emergency room physician and former Arizona legislator, lost to Republican David Schweikert by 3.8 points in the district in 2024, Axios reported. The district includes Scottsdale, parts of northeast Phoenix, Fountain Hills and Cave Creek. Feely, a longtime Gilbert resident, switched from the 5th district race to the 1st at Trump’s urging, according to Axios. The two clashed over data centres at a recent Clean Elections debate, ABC15 reported. “When I’m talking to the voters, what they have said to me clearly is they don’t want them in CD-1,” Shah said. Feely argued that data centres help the economy. “They add about a billion dollars in revenue to the state of Arizona. That’s giving you the opportunity to increase teacher’s pay,” he said. He accused Shah of changing his position. “I think it’s really hypocritical for you to stand up here and say to the voters that you’re now against data centers. When you were in office, you voted for the tax credits to bring those data centers here,” Feely said. Shah said artificial intelligence was not on the radar when that vote was taken. “However, when the situation changes and suddenly you’ve got massive amounts of people applying as we have seen, and you see that you’re going to double the amount of wattage that these things are going to take. You’re going to have to think about the ratepayers,” he said. Despite the district’s Republican registration advantage, the Cook Political Report rates the race “lean Democratic” and Inside Elections calls it “tilt Democratic”, Axios reported. Republicans make up 38 per cent of registered voters, against 35 per cent independent or other parties and over 26 per cent Democrats. “If independents show up in big numbers, it favors Shah. If they don’t, it favors Feely,” pollster Marcus Dell’Artino told the Arizona Capitol Times, as quoted by Axios. Federal filings show heavy outside spending on both sides, including $5.72 million by the MAGA Inc.-funded Safety & Affordability PAC against Shah and $4.41 million by House Majority PAC against Feely. The last day for Arizona voters to request an early ballot was October 23. The general election is on November 3.

news.title: Trump calls Iran war costs 'small price to pay'
news.text: Digital Desk | Washington, Oct 24 (IANS) US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that the war with Iran has driven up oil prices and added to the financial pressures facing American households, but defended the economic consequences as a necessary price for preventing Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons. In an interview with Florida television station WINK-TV, Trump said he had anticipated an increase in energy prices when he decided to launch military operations against Iran. He insisted that the conflict would end soon and predicted that petrol prices would fall rapidly. His remarks came as Americans prepared for the November 3 midterm elections, with the cost of living emerging as a major political issue and Republicans fighting to retain control of Congress. "You know, it's a small price to pay for taking a nuclear weapon away from Iran, which is a very evil country," Trump said when asked about the financial burden on consumers. The President was responding to a question from WINK-TV anchor Claire Galt, who pointed out that Americans continued to face high grocery bills and that petrol prices in southwest Florida had reached an average of $4.18 a gallon. Trump acknowledged that beef prices remained elevated and that oil prices had risen because of the conflict. "Beef's a little bit high and it's coming down," he said, adding that cattle production meant prices could take longer to adjust. Turning to energy, Trump said he had expected the increase but considered military action unavoidable. "We had it very low and I knew that would happen, but it was a choice," he said. The President maintained that Iran posed an unacceptable nuclear threat and argued that previous American administrations should have acted earlier. "Number one state sponsor of terror, they can't have a nuclear weapon. Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. So, I'm honored to have done it," he said. Trump offered no specific timetable for ending the conflict but suggested that a negotiated settlement was not the only possible outcome. "I see it ending soon. I see it ending one way or another, through agreement or otherwise," he said. The remarks left open the possibility of further military action even as the administration sought to reassure Americans about the economic consequences of the war. At a separate Republican campaign rally in Fort Myers, Trump returned to the subject and said his administration had weighed the likely economic impact before proceeding with military operations. He recalled seeing petrol prices of $1.85 and $1.95 a gallon during a visit to Iowa before the military campaign. Trump said he subsequently told senior administration officials that preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons had to take priority. He also claimed that oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz had increased despite the conflict. "Tremendous amounts of oil are coming through the Hormuz Strait, more than we actually had before the war, which is pretty amazing," he said in the television interview. The President attributed the movement of oil shipments to American military operations and the US Navy's presence in the region. His claims about shipping volumes were not independently verified in the supplied material.

news.title: Vanessa Trump, 48, breaks silence on cancer battle with emotional health update
news.text:
Vanessa Trump has shared the wonderful news that she is cancer-free, six months after being diagnosed with breast cancer.

The 48-year-old former model, who is dating golf legend Tiger Woods, revealed the update in an emotional video shared by her eldest daughter, Kai Trump, on Instagram on Friday, October 23.

Vanessa, who was previously married to Donald Trump Jr., appeared alongside Kai, 19, as they discussed her health journey in honour of Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

"My mom was diagnosed with breast cancer in April," Kai explained at the beginning of the video.

"So we thought we would share her story and how she was diagnosed and how she overcame it."

Vanessa then revealed that her latest medical tests had delivered the news she had been hoping for.

"It came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free," she announced, before sharing a warm embrace with her daughter.

The mother-daughter duo also sat down with Dr Nicole Saphier to discuss Vanessa's diagnosis, treatment and recovery, with a longer conversation set to be released on Kai's YouTube channel.

Alongside the video, Kai explained that they hoped sharing her mother's experience would raise awareness about breast cancer and the importance of early detection.

Vanessa first publicly revealed her diagnosis in May, explaining that she was working closely with her medical team on a treatment plan.

In a statement shared on Instagram, the mother-of-five confirmed that she had undergone a medical procedure and was grateful for the support of her doctors and loved ones.

"I am staying focused and hopeful," she wrote at the time, adding that she was surrounded by her children, family and those closest to her.

The announcement prompted an outpouring of support, including from her former sister-in-law Ivanka Trump, who offered prayers for her recovery.

In June, Vanessa shared another update, revealing that she was recovering from surgery and preparing to begin the next stage of treatment.

Throughout her health battle, Vanessa has been supported by her five children, Kai, Donald III, Tristan, Spencer and Chloe, whom she shares with her ex-husband Donald Trump Jr. The former couple married in 2005 before divorcing in 2018.

Vanessa has also had the support of her boyfriend, Tiger Woods, 50, whom she began dating in 2024.

The couple made their relationship public in March 2025, when the golfing champion shared photographs of them together on Instagram.

Vanessa's latest announcement marks a welcome milestone for the family after months of treatment, with the mother-of-five now using her experience to encourage greater breast cancer awareness.
news.summary: Vanessa Trump has announced she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis in April. The mother-of-five shared the news in an emotional video with daughter Kai Trump.

news.title: Britt McHenry quits Trump role after being 'booted' from NBA game for throwing drink
news.text: A Trump official has resigned just 24 hours after receiving a promotion, following her removal from a packed basketball stadium while crowds of supporters jeered her exit. Britt McHenry forfeited her US government position after allegedly hurling a drink over a fellow spectator at an NBA basketball fixture in Washington. The former ESPN journalist was reportedly pushed into resigning from her role with Donald Trump on Thursday, October 22, after video footage surfaced online. It depicted her throwing a drink at a spectator during the Washington Wizards' home opener the previous evening. McHenry left just one day after she was reportedly promoted to head External Affairs and Press for Under Secretary Jacob Helberg's team. The reported resignation followed a heated confrontation at Capital One Arena on Wednesday, after McHenry witnessed Washington defeat the Milwaukee Bucks 128-116. NBA supporters booed as she exited the arena with some tossing rally towels in her direction, while she waved and blew kisses back at the crowd. One insider described it as: "promoted and fired in 24 hours." The State Department declined to comment on the complete details surrounding her departure or why she left the match early. DC YouTuber Andrew Fenichel was standing next to McHenry when the incident occurred. He swiftly dismissed rumours that he was romantically involved with her or that he supported Trump after fans bombarded him with furious messages. "Britt is not my girlfriend. There's no romantic history there at all. Britt and I are just friends," he said, before adding, "Guys, I'm not MAGA, okay?" The altercation reportedly began when men seated behind McHenry taunted Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma and made offensive remarks about his fiancée, model Winnie Harlow. McHenry allegedly attempted to quieten them down, which is said to have triggered the confrontation. Eyewitnesses claimed the group directed abuse at McHenry and threw a drink at her first. Video footage appeared to capture part of the exchange, though not every detail was clearly visible. Clips then showed McHenry hurling a drink back at the fans as the situation escalated. Arena staff escorted her out while the crowd jeered and threw objects in her direction. McHenry was heard asking a security guard, "What'd I do?". Accounts varied as to whether she was officially ejected or departed of her own accord. Those supporting McHenry maintained she chose to head to a bar, while footage appeared to show security staff guiding her away from the area. McHenry had previously taken to Instagram to announce her new government role following her appointment, describing it as an honour to serve. She has since disabled comments on her account. Prior to her venture into politics, McHenry had established her career at ESPN. She joined the administration in September as a press adviser for Europe and Africa, according to Page Six.
news.summary: Britt McHenry lost her Trump administration role after apparently throwing a drink at a fellow spectator at a Washington Wizards NBA game at Capital One Arena

news.title: US authorises emergency release of up to 400,000 oil barrels
news.text:
WASHINGTON: The US Department of Energy said on Friday it had authorised an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66’s Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.

The SPR is already at the lowest level since 1982 after President Donald Trump tapped it as the US war on Iran disrupted supply lines, and after his predecessor, President Joe Biden, turned to it following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The Lake Charles refinery has a capacity to refine about 264,000 barrels per day.

The exchange will “help offset temporary disruptions affecting crude oil deliveries to the refinery and support continued production of transportation fuels serving Louisiana and surrounding markets,” the department said.

The refinery will receive crude oil from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, a Phillips 66 spokesperson confirmed on Friday, but he declined to comment on refinery operations or commercial activity. “We do not anticipate impacts to Lake Charles operations,” he said.

news.title: Oil hits USD116 mark as ME conflict rages on
news.text:
NEW YORK: Oil prices settled more than USD3 higher on Friday, their highest in nearly six months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where UAE authorities also reported an oil spill.

Brent crude futures settled at USD116.72 a barrel, up USD3.55 or 3.14 percent, their highest since April 29. US West Texas Intermediate crude closed at USD103.27 a barrel, up USD3.80 or 3.8 percent.

Brent finished the week up 6 percent and WTI ended 2.3 percent higher.

“Fears of supply disruptions drove the advance after Houthi carried out a series of attacks across Saudi Arabia, including on energy infrastructure,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for LPL Financial.

On Thursday, Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters reported. Fighting intensified between Saudi Arabia, the world’s largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis.

An oil spill from a tanker was detected off the UAE coast of Umm Al Quwain, the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said. It did not say what caused the spill and authorities have not identified the tanker involved.

Shipping sources said on October 9 that the Gem No. 2 supertanker was struck by an unidentified projectile 13 nautical miles (24 km) west of Al Jazeera in the UAE.

“The market is concerned about these continued Iranian attacks on tankers that we’ve seen increase over the last week,” said Andrew Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates. “While there has been an increase in oil transiting out of the Strait of Hormuz, that could change at any minute.”

Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government have raged since the Houthis pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb Strait last month, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea.

October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017.

President Donald Trump said on Friday the US could end the war with Iran quickly, but said perhaps Washington should allow the conflict to gradually wind down.

The US Department of Energy said it had authorized an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66’s Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.

The SPR is already at the lowest level since 1982 after President Donald Trump tapped it as the US war on Iran disrupted supply lines. Trump’s predecessor, President Joe Biden, also tapped the SPR following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Elsewhere, Germany’s national oil stockpiling agency EBV circulated a tender to sell diesel, heating oil and crude oil volumes from strategic reserves.

This marks Germany’s first oil releases from strategic reserves since G7 countries, under pressure from Trump, agreed to do so at the start of October.

On Thursday, the head of Libya’s National Oil Corp told Reuters that an oil pipeline valve from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port had been shut, leading to a reduction in production at both fields.

Ship tracking data showed the first Russian diesel bound for the US since Moscow and Washington reached an export agreement was aboard a tanker heading for New York.

Trump announced the deal this month as part of efforts to bring down soaring diesel prices ahead of US midterm elections on November 3.

US energy firms this week kept the total rig count unchanged for a second week in a row, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, held steady at 603 during the week ended October 23.

news.title: Defense attorneys in Charlie Kirk’s killing want to have a trial in 2029
news.text:
Defense attorneys for the Utah man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk said they need several years to prepare their case and suggested a 2029 trial date.

An attorney for Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk, called the proposal “absurd” and accused defendant Tyler Robinson of trying to delay.

Utah District Court Judge Tony Graf had been expected to set the trial date during a Friday hearing. However, no date was set and Graf scheduled the next hearing for Nov. 9.

Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in last year’s killing of Kirk as the 31-year-old activist spoke to several thousand people at Utah Valley University. The defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting, and his lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk’s death.

He could be eligible for the death penalty if convicted.

Kirk helped galvanize youth voters around President Donald Trump during the 2024 election. Trump weighed in on the case in a social media post prior to Friday’s hearing. He said it should be tried “within a month.” Trump criticized Graf — a former prosecutor appointed as a judge last year — for “taking forever to ask questions that people already know the answer to.”

Utah County prosecutors allege the 23-year-old defendant targeted Kirk for his political beliefs. They say a bullet found in the rifle used to kill Kirk was engraved with “Hey Facist! CATCH!” and that Robinson wrote in a text message about Kirk: “I had enough of his hatred. Some hate can’t be negotiated out.”

Prosecutors said they anticipate a 17-week trial and would be ready by October 2027. But rather than hold the proceedings during the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, they proposed the trial begin in January 2028.

Erika Kirk’s attorney said the trial should start next October. Dragging it out for years would violate her speedy trial rights under Utah law as a victim, said attorney Jeffrey Neiman.

“Under the Defendants’ proposed schedule, Mr. Kirk’s two children, who were one and three at the time he was murdered, will be six and eight years old by the time the trial concludes,” Neiman wrote in a court filing. “They will face the uncertainty of this criminal proceeding longer than they had their father in their lives.”

Robinson’s attorneys said in court filings this week that they must sift through tens of thousands of files turned over by prosecutors. They plan extensive investigations into Robinson’s life in a search for mitigating factors that could influence his sentence if convicted, and to devote “substantial time” to issues such as jury selection.

news.title: Trump Threatens Iran Strike — ‘We May Do Another Little Epic Fury’
news.text:
President Donald Trump warned Friday that the United States could launch another round of military strikes against Iran unless Tehran reaches an agreement, escalating his threats as Washington intensifies economic pressure on the Islamic Republic.

“We may do another little Epic Fury, or they’ll agree,” Trump told supporters at a midterm campaign rally in Fort Myers, Florida, referring to the U.S. military operation launched against Iran in February.

“If they’re smart, they’ll just say, ‘Let’s get down to business.’ But, you know, I doubt they’ll do that because perhaps they’re not smart,” he added.

The remarks marked Trump’s latest warning of renewed military action against Tehran, following his declaration Thursday that American forces had already “knocked the hell out of” Iran and might go “a little bit further.”

Earlier Friday, Trump asserted that the United States controlled the Strait of Hormuz, allowing other countries to ship oil through the strategic waterway while restricting Iran’s own exports.

“The question is, do we want to finish it off, or do we just want to let it wither? Because we’re getting everything we want,” Trump told reporters.

He went further in a separate exchange, suggesting that the United States possessed the military capability to seize Iran’s oil resources or even the country itself.

“We could take the whole country. We could take all of the oil,” he said. “And as you know, the Hormuz Strait is totally ours, and that’s the way we’ll keep it.”

The president’s remarks came as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declared that American efforts to isolate Iran economically had devastated its oil-export network while allowing energy shipments from the wider Persian Gulf to recover.

“Despite Iran’s efforts to disrupt energy shipments, oil exports from the Persian Gulf are roaring back and have surpassed pre-conflict levels,” Bessent wrote Friday.

“The message is clear: Iran’s threats have failed to stop the flow of energy to global markets,” he added.

In a separate statement earlier Friday, Bessent credited the administration’s Operation Economic Outcast with depleting Iran’s shadow tanker fleet, emptying its main oil terminal and exhausting its offshore reserves.

“As President Trump takes action that his predecessors long deferred, the United States is no longer managing the Iranian threat. We are ending it,” he declared.

Trump’s remarks also reflected the competing approaches to Iran detailed in a Thursday report by The Atlantic, which described Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent advocating sustained economic pressure while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged Trump to pursue another round of devastating strikes aimed at toppling the Iranian regime.

According to the report, the Trump administration is considering combining the two strategies, potentially launching several days of strikes after the November midterm elections against Iranian missile and drone capabilities, energy infrastructure and nuclear facilities. An outside adviser cited in the report argued that economic pressure had brought Iran close to collapse and that additional strikes “would push them over.”

The prospect of more immediate military action surfaced Friday when U.S. Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack suggested that American forces could strike Iran as soon as this weekend.

“Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely,” Barrack said during an interview with Mario Nawfal, while emphasizing that Trump remained open to a negotiated agreement.

Asked about Barrack’s remarks before his Florida rally, Trump appeared to playfully question the ambassador’s authority to predict military action.

“That’s my ambassador to Turkey. He’s a pretty powerful man, I guess,” Trump quipped.

“If that’s the case, I don’t know anything about it,” he added.

The president appeared to dismiss Barrack’s suggestion of an imminent strike without ruling out further military action.

Meanwhile, Iran has warned of retaliation if Washington resumes its military campaign.

Reuters reported Friday that two senior Iranian security officials described contingency plans to attack undersea communications cables in the Persian Gulf, including efforts to prevent repairs and prolong disruptions.

“If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines … from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones,” one official warned.

Separately, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Brig. Gen. Yadollah Javani threatened that Iran would become a killing ground for foreign troops if the United States attempted a ground invasion.

The escalating warnings come as Washington moves diplomatic personnel and family members out of several Middle Eastern countries. CNN reported Friday that the State Department had quietly adjusted staffing at embassies in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Lebanon, in addition to ordering the departure of non-emergency personnel and family members from Saudi Arabia amid intensified attacks by the Iranian-backed Houthis.

Despite the heightened tensions, the administration continues to insist that a diplomatic agreement remains possible.

U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz said Friday that the American blockade could be maintained for the foreseeable future and that Washington’s pressure campaign was intensifying, while emphasizing that decisions about the duration of the confrontation and any further military action ultimately rest with Trump.

“The president and the U.S. Navy can maintain this blockade for their foreseeable future. The maximum pressure campaign is only tightening,” Waltz said.
